title: The Man Who Drew the Universe
working_title: The Man Who Drew the Universe
subtitle: Richard Feynman — a life in curiosity and physics
based_on: the documented life and scientific work of Richard Phillips Feynman (1918-1988) — ORIGINAL NARRATIVE ACCOUNT of the events, not a derivative of any single existing biography's text
setting: Far Rockaway, MIT, Princeton, Los Alamos, Cornell, Caltech, Stockholm, Washington D.C. — 1918-1988
logline: A radio-repair kid from a working-class corner of Queens talks his way past every gate physics puts up, helps build the bomb that ends a war he then can't stop grieving his young wife inside, redraws quantum electrodynamics as pictures a technician can use, and spends the rest of a Nobel-Prize life insisting that the pleasure of finding things out is the only prize that ever mattered.
blueprint: cradle-to-grave narrative biography in scenes — Far Rockaway and the father's kitchen-table science, MIT and Princeton, Los Alamos and Arline, the postwar collapse and the Cornell wobbling-plate turn, the diagrams and Shelter Island, Caltech and the Lectures, Stockholm, the showman years, the Challenger commission, the last illness — closing on an epilogue of what the diagrams and the lectures left behind
market: readers of Genius-style scientist biographies, Surely You're Joking's audience who want the fuller and more sober frame around the stories, popular-physics readers, teachers
tone: warm, exact, unsentimental about the science and honest about the cost of the life; curiosity as the load-bearing virtue, showmanship never mistaken for the whole man
dedication: For everyone who was ever told to stop asking why.
clearances: Feynman died in 1988 (long deceased, public figure of major historical record) -> depictable; Arline Greenbaum Feynman (d. 1945), Mary Louise Bell (d. 2012), and Gweneth Howarth Feynman (d. 1989) likewise long deceased. This is an ORIGINAL narrative account built from the well-documented public record (interviews, the Nobel archive, the Rogers Commission record, and the biographical consensus); no sentence is copied from Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!, What Do You Care What Other People Think?, or any Feynman biography — dialogue and interior monologue are reconstructed in the author's own words, kept true to the documented frame, exactly as this house's practice requires for every true story on this shelf.
sensitivity_read: not required — public figure, scientific and historical record, no living-person exposure
